# CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Support

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading, a configuration that can run with the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) disabled. In this configuration, an application’s runtime choice also affects what happens when it imports extensions.

An extension must explicitly indicate that it supports free threading. If it does not, importing it produces a warning and enables the GIL. The way to declare support differs between extensions that use multi-phase initialization and those that use single-phase initialization.

There are also build and configuration details to account for. On Windows, the compiler does not automatically receive the `Py_GIL_DISABLED` macro; the configuration can be checked through `sysconfig`.

The declaration is a compatibility signal that affects import behavior, not proof that an extension’s code is thread-safe. Extension authors therefore have a distinct responsibility to indicate support, while the declaration itself does not establish thread safety.
